paragraph: Angola's Lei n.º 22/11 on personal data protection was [published on 17 June 2011](<https://lex.ao/docs/assembleia-nacional/2011/lei-n-o-22-11-de-17-de-junho/>). The Agência de Protecção de Dados was set up by [Decreto Presidencial n.º 214/16](<https://lex.ao/docs/presidente-da-republica/2016/decreto-presidencial-n-o-214-16-de-10-de-outubro/>). In [June 2026](<https://angop.ao/noticias/politica/parlamento-rejeita-proposta-sobre-proteccao-de-dados-pessoais/>) the Assembleia Nacional rejected a bill to amend the law. Its [register of fines](<https://apd.ao/ao/gca/index.php?id=218&preview=1>) lists 15 fines for 2022 to 2026. In the last twelve months, on [10 August 2026](<https://sapo.pt/artigo/agencia-de-proteccao-de-dados-de-angola-multa-hotel-diamante-em-115-mil-dolares-6a857707bf642b2fcc16d93b>) the authority fined Lizária, Lda., owner of Hotel Diamante, the kwanza equivalent of USD 115,000 under Deliberação n.º 006/2026.

Burundi's National Assembly unanimously [adopted a bill on personal data protection on 15 January 2026](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/burundi-lawmakers-approve-data-protection-framework-as-digitalisation-accelerates>). In the last twelve months the position changed from [DLA Piper's guide of 17 January 2024](<https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?c=BI&t=law>), which described only sector confidentiality provisions and no national authority. Community Voice reports that the head of state [promulgated the law on 10 March 2026](<https://communityvoice.bi/1489-2/>). The law [establishes an independent administrative authority](<https://communityvoice.bi/1489-2/>). The [African Union's status list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records no signature of the Malabo Convention. No source has been found saying the law is in force or the authority constituted. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

Benin's personal data protection sits in Book V of the Digital Code, [law no. 2017-20 of 20 April 2018](<https://archive.apdp.bj/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Rapport-Bilan_2015-2020_Version-finale.pdf>), [amended by law no. 2020-35 of 6 January 2021](<https://sgg.gouv.bj/doc/decret-2022-107/>). Benin [ratified the Malabo Convention on 14 May 2024](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>). The APDP's [2025 report](<https://www.lanation.bj/numerique/protection-des-donnees-personnelles-en-2025-au-benin-lapdp-dresse-un-bilan-sous-le-signe-de-la-conformite>) gives 907 files examined, 64 inspection missions, 20 complaints treated and 75 compliance certificates issued. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

Law no. 001-2021/AN of 30 March 2021 [abrogates law no. 010-2004/AN](<https://www.fonction-publique.gov.bf/fileadmin/user_upload/storage/22-08-2021-C2-LOI-N__001-2021_AN_portant_protection_des_personnes.pdf>) on personal data protection in Burkina Faso. In the last twelve months, on 3 August 2026 deputies [adopted the law creating ARCOD](<https://www.aib.media/burkina-les-deputes-adoptent-la-loi-portant-creation-de-larcod-issue-de-la-fusion-du-csc-et-de-la-cil/>), which merges the CIL and the CSC. By decree of 16 October 2026 [the CSC's president, Wendingoudi Louis Modeste Ouedraogo, was named president of ARCOD](<https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article150089>). [On 19 November 2026 the government named the ten councillors of its first college](<https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article150924=>). No act of ARCOD has been found, and no ruling against a named organisation in the last three years. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

Botswana's [Data Protection Act No. 18 of 2024](<https://itlawco.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/1736836435941.pdf>) came into operation on 14 January 2025. In the last twelve months, [Mmegi reports](<https://www.mmegi.bw/business/new-data-commission-tightens-compliance-oversight/news>) Kepaletswe Somolekae as the newly appointed Information and Data Protection Commissioner on 11 February 2026. On 17 July 2026 the Commission [issued a Determination and an Enforcement Notice](<https://na.co.bw/data-commission-orders-suspension-of-dpsm-epayslip-portal-over-privacy-law-breaches/>) against DPSM. It ordered the ePayslip portal suspended and a DPIA and revised privacy notice submitted within one month. [Mmegi reports](<https://www.mmegi.bw/news/govt-e-payslip-fails-data-protection-compliance-test/news>) DPSM suspended the portal on 22 July 2026.

[Data Protection Africa states](<https://dataprotection.africa/central-african-republic>) in its factsheet of 28 January 2026 that the Central African Republic has a data protection law in place. The [promulgated text of Loi n° 24.001](<https://blog.africadataprotection.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Loi_24_001_portant_protection_des_donnes_a_caractere__personnel.pdf>) was adopted in January 2024 and gives no commencement date. [Article 57](<https://blog.africadataprotection.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Loi_24_001_portant_protection_des_donnes_a_caractere__personnel.pdf>) gives the ministry in charge of the digital economy a set period to set up the data protection agency. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found saying the Malabo Convention is signed or ratified, or that an authority has been appointed. Establishing would need ratification of the Malabo Convention or an appointed authority.

Côte d'Ivoire's [law of 19 June 2013 on personal data protection](<https://www.artci.ci/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/decret_2015_79.pdf>) is the framework for a 2015 decree on filing fees and prior authorisations. In the last twelve months, ARTCI [launched Certinum on 2 July 2026](<https://www.fratmat.info/article/2642985/economie/ntic/protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-certinum-entre-en-service-pour-accelerer-la-conformite-numerique-en-cote-divoire>), an online platform for compliance and authorisation requests. It replaces about 100 paper files a month. ARTCI [issued a communique on 3 August 2026](<https://artci.ci/lartci-invite-les-entreprises-a-privilegier-la-plateforme-certinum/>) inviting controllers to use it. By then it had [received 210 complaints and carried out 18 inspections](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/0707-139967-cote-divoire-ce-que-certinum-va-changer-pour-les-entreprises-et-les-administrations>). No ruling by the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

Cameroon's Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 governs personal data protection. The [Direction Generale du Budget states](<https://www.dgb.cm/la-loi-sur-la-protection-des-donnees-personnelles-entre-officiellement-en-vigueur/>) that its deadline for entry into force was reached on 23 June 2026. The [law](<https://prc.cm/fr/multimedia/documents/10258-loi-n-2024-017-du-23-12-2024-web>) makes the Autorité an independent public body with supervision and enforcement powers. In the last twelve months, on 29 October 2026 [CLG Global said](<https://clgglobal.com/cameroons-ai-data-centre-five-legal-questions-before-the-first-server-is-installed/>) it was not yet operational. It awaited a presidential decree, with no head or members appointed. The African Union Commission's [status list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records that Cameroon signed the Convention on 12 August 2021. Establishing would need ratification of the Malabo Convention or an appointed authority.

DR Congo's [Digital Code, Ordinance-Law No. 23/010 of 13 March 2023](<https://droitnumerique.cd/arptic-arptc-investie-des-missions-de-lautorite-de-protection-des-donnees-en-rd-congo/>), entered into force in 2023 and provides for the Autorité de Protection des Données. A [ministerial order of 17 August 2024](<https://droitnumerique.cd/autorite-de-protection-des-donnees/>) gave the authority's missions to the telecoms regulator, ARPTC, until the authority is set up. In the last twelve months, the ARPTC's [decision on prior formalities under the Code was published in the Journal officiel on 23 April 2026](<https://www.africadataprotection.org/rdc-publication-au-journal-officiel-de-la-decision-fixant-la-procedure-des-formalites-prealables.html>). It sets how organisations declare their processing. [Beto.cd reported on 13 September 2026](<https://beto.cd/onip-rgph2-deux-comptages-population-autorite-protection-donnees/>) that the Autorité itself is not installed. No ruling by the ARPTC against a named organisation has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

Congo's [Law No. 29-2019 of 10 October 2019 on personal data protection](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/01/22/congo-launches-commission-to-strengthen-personal-data-protection-and-digital-governance/>) is in force as of 22 January 2026. In the last twelve months, the National Personal Data Protection Commission was inaugurated in January 2026 when its members were [appointed under Decree No. 2025-538 of 31 December 2025](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/01/22/congo-launches-commission-to-strengthen-personal-data-protection-and-digital-governance/>). On 22 January 2026 [ITWeb Africa reported](<https://itweb.africa/article/congo-brazzaville-intros-data-protection-commission/>) that ICT minister Leon Juste Ibombo installed its members. No source dated in the last three years has been found. None shows it registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting. Operating would need an appointed authority that has done one of those things in the past three years.

[TechHive Advisory states](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-the-comoros-data-protection-law>) the Union of Comoros enacted its Protection of Personal Data Law on 29 June 2021. The [Assembly adopted Loi n°14-029/AU](<https://anaden.org/uploads/media/63076edf43d1e/loi-portant-sur-la-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-de-lunion-des-comores.pdf>) on personal data protection on 26 June 2014. [Article 19 of the 2014 law](<https://anaden.org/uploads/media/63076edf43d1e/loi-portant-sur-la-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-de-lunion-des-comores.pdf>) institutes a Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés, and TechHive says the authority had not been formally constituted as of mid-2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found showing that the law has commenced, or that the authority has been constituted since. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

[The CNPD president says](<https://expressodasilhas.cv/pais/2025/02/02/a-ia-ou-o-big-data-nao-podem-por-em-causa-os-direitos-das-pessoas/95448>) the base data protection law of Cabo Verde dates from 2001. It was amended in 2013 and again [on 17 March 2021](<https://rlpd.org/cnpd-cabo-verde-um-percurso-de-onze-anos/>). The CNPD's members [took office on 24 April 2015](<https://rlpd.org/cnpd-cabo-verde-um-percurso-de-onze-anos/>). [Resolução n.º 160/X/2024](<https://www.mf.gov.cv/documents/198414/4674538/Lei%20que%20aprova%20o%20OE%202025.pdf>) gives it CVE 36,313,115 for 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

The National Assembly passed Djibouti's first [Digital Code](<https://www.jonesday.com/en/insights/2025/07/national-assembly-of-the-republic-of-djibouti-approves-digital-code>), with a data-protection regime embedded in it, on 30 June 2025. It was still to be promulgated by the President and published in the Journal Officiel. The Code creates the [National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-djiboutis-data-protection-law>). On 9 November 2023 the Assembly [adopted law 18/AN/23 ratifying the Convention](<https://www.journalofficiel.dj/texte-juridique/loi-n-18-an-23-9eme-ll-portant-ratification-de-la-convention-de-lunion-africaine-sur-la-cybersecurite-et-la-protection-de-donnees-a-caractere-personnel/>), but the [African Union status list](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) of 2 February 2026 records only a signature. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found giving when the Code was promulgated or took effect. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

The [US International Trade Administration](<https://www.trade.gov/country-commercial-guides/algeria-digital-economy>) states that Algeria's Law No. 18-07, enacted on 10 June 2018, came into force on 10 August 2023. In the last twelve months, the national authority, the ANPDP, adopted a [deliberation](<https://anpdp.dz/ar/storage/2026/07/MOD-19-07-2026-v2.pdf>) on 15 July 2026, with twelve members named. On 11 November 2026 it [announced Deliberation No. 05, setting rules for personal data in CVs under Law 18-07](<https://www.lesoirdalgerie.com/actualites/l-anpdp-encadre-le-traitement-des-informations-contenues-dans-les-cv-160122>). [Tech Hive Advisory](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/bimonthly-update-on-privacy-in-africa-january-february-2026>) reports a decision in early 2026 on employee drug test results. No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

[Shura Law Firm](<https://shuralawfirm.com/en/egypt-pdpl-compliance-checklist-what-to-do-before-the-october-31-2026-deadline/>) says Egypt's Law No. 151 of 2020 entered into force in October 2020. Its [executive regulations are dated 1 November 2025](<https://www.actpol.org/research/egypt-data-protection-deadline-north-africa>) and give organisations a year to comply. In the last twelve months, [Tech Hive Advisory](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/bimonthly-update-on-privacy-in-africa-january-february-2026>) says the Personal Data Protection Centre published guidelines in January and February 2026, with breach-notification templates. [Baker McKenzie](<https://www.bakermckenzie.com/en/insight/publications/2026/10/egypt-personal-data-protection-law-update>) says the Centre opened an electronic portal in early October 2026 for licence and permit applications. A [7 August 2026 report](<https://gate.ahram.org.eg/Massai/News/5884624.aspx>) still names an acting chief executive. No ruling by the Centre against a named organisation has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

[Law Lab Africa](<https://research.lawlab.africa/eritrea/>) states that no comprehensive data protection law is in force in Eritrea, as of a verification pass on 1 August 2026. A June 2025 [Horn of Africa Initiative update](<https://hoainitiative.org/sites/default/files/2025-09/25th%20HoAI%20Ministerial%20-%20Background%20Paper%20on%20Digital%20Integration%20Update.pdf>) says Eritrea remains without data protection legislation. Law Lab Africa also states that no supervisory authority has been established. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The [African Union status list](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) of 2 February 2026 records no signature of the Malabo Convention by Eritrea. No draft data protection law has been found. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

Ethiopia published its [Personal Data Protection Proclamation](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-ethiopias-data-protection-act>) in the Federal Negarit Gazette on 24 July 2024. [Shega reported in November 2025](<https://shega.co/news/one-year-on-ethiopia-s-personal-data-protection-law-faces-a-slow-path-to-enforcement>) that it took effect on publication. [The Tech Hive review](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-ethiopias-data-protection-act>) says the Ethiopian Communications Authority is the regulator under Article 5. In November 2025 its Director General said data processors and collectors now need the Authority's permission. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

[Loi n°025/2023](<https://www.apdpvp.ga/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Gabon-Loi-025-2023-du-12-juillet-2023-portant-modification-de-la-loi-001-2011-du-25-septembre-relative-a-la-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel.pdf>) of 12 July 2023 amended Gabon's 2011 data protection law. The APDPVP's president, vice-president and six other commissioners were [appointed by the Council of Ministers on 12 July 2023](<https://www.apdpvp.ga/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/SANCTION-CITIBANK-25-AVRIL-2024.pdf>). In the last twelve months, its president [gave its review of 2025](<https://www.gabonreview.com/journee-mondiale-de-la-protection-des-donnees-le-gabon-affirme-sa-strategie-face-aux-defis-du-numerique/>) on 27 January 2026, counting 12 administrative and financial sanctions on controllers in breach in 2025. By September 2026 it had logged [about 715 declarations of conformity and about 30 complaints](<https://union.sonapresse.com/fr/joel-dominique-ledaga-pour-echanger-directement-avec-meta-tiktok-ou-instagram-il-faut-une-reponse>).

The [Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843)](<https://gna.org.gh/2026/10/dpc-begins-checks-on-data-protection-compliance/>) is the law Ghana's Data Protection Commission enforces in 2026. In the last twelve months, in [August 2026](<https://gna.org.gh/2026/08/data-protection-commission-acquires-vehicles-to-boost-nationwide-enforcement/>) the Commission declared 2026 the 'Year of Enforcement'. It [registered 2,575 data controllers in 2026](<https://gna.org.gh/2026/10/dpc-strengthens-enforcement-after-registering-2575-data-controllers/>). On 12 October 2026 it [directed Nyaho Medical Centre to report to the Police CID](<https://www.myjoyonline.com/nyaho-medical-centre-referred-to-cid-over-allegedly-expired-data-protection-registration/>) over an expired registration certificate. On 20 October 2026 it [warned a ministry and media houses](<https://gna.org.gh/2026/10/dpc-warns-against-disclosure-of-evacuated-ghanaians-personal-data/>) over disclosing evacuees' personal data. No count of the Commission's rulings has been found.

Guinea's [2016 cybersecurity and personal data protection law, Loi L/2016/037/AN](<https://anssi.gov.gn/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/loi_l2016037an_relative_a_la_cybersecurite_et_protection_des_do.pdf>), was adopted and promulgated by President Alpha Condé. The law [defines an Autorité de Protection and sets its functions](<https://assembleeguinee.org/loi-ndeg-l-2016-relative-la-cybersecurite-et-la-protection-des-donnees-caractere-personnel-en>). The CNT reported on [20 June 2024](<https://cnt.gov.gn/apdp/>) that its commissions debated a bill to establish the authority, and that the designation of members was still contested. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No authority constituted or appointed has been found. Operating would need an appointed authority that has registered organisations, taken breach reports, issued guidance or inspected in the past three years.

President Barrow [assented to the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2025 on 7 November 2025](<https://www.africanlawbusiness.com/expert-views/key-features-of-the-gambian-personal-data-protection-and-privacy-act/>). No grace period and no commencement date are given. In the last twelve months, a notice of 17 August 2026 says the [Information Commission of The Gambia is to develop a communication strategy](<https://gambia.unfpa.org/en/vacancies/development-communication-strategy-information-commission-gambia>) to raise awareness of the Act. The Gambia [signed the Convention on 2 December 2022](<https://mocde.gov.gm/3189-2/>). The [African Union's list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records signature and no ratification. No commencement date for the Act has been found. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

A [professor at the Bissau Faculty of Law said on 22 September 2026 that Guinea-Bissau does not yet have specific data protection legislation](<https://www.aip.ci/cote-divoire-aip-inter-la-cour-de-justice-de-la-cedeao-dispose-dun-cadre-pour-statuer-sur-les-droits-numeriques-selon-un-universitaire/>). A [national report of 18 February 2025](<https://upr-info.org/sites/default/files/country-document/2025-09/A_HRC_WG.6_49_GNB_1_F.pdf>) lists a personal data protection bill awaiting discussion. The professor [said Guinea-Bissau has no dedicated national data protection authority](<https://www.aip.ci/cote-divoire-aip-inter-la-cour-de-justice-de-la-cedeao-dispose-dun-cadre-pour-statuer-sur-les-droits-numeriques-selon-un-universitaire/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The [African Union's status list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records that Guinea-Bissau signed the Malabo Convention on 31 January 2015 and had not ratified it. The stage of the bill has not been found. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

[Ley Núm. 1/2016 of 22 July 2016](<https://blog.africadataprotection.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Guinee-equatoriale-ley-1-2.016-de-proteccion-de-datos.pdf>) sets rules for personal data processing in Equatorial Guinea. [Articles 15 and 29 name the Órgano Rector de Protección de Datos Personales as the supervisory body](<https://blog.africadataprotection.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Guinee-equatoriale-ley-1-2.016-de-proteccion-de-datos.pdf>), to be created by a decree. In the last twelve months, the African Union's Infrastructure and Energy Department reports that [Equatorial Guinea's foreign minister signed the Malabo Convention in Addis Ababa on 28 July 2026](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/au-infrastructure-and-energy_equatorial-guinea-signs-the-malabo-convention-activity-7488275982521565184-ETtI>). No ratification of the Convention has been found. No appointment to the authority and no ruling against an organisation has been found. Establishing would need ratification of the Malabo Convention or an appointed authority.

Kenya's Office of the Data Protection Commissioner was [established under the Data Protection Act, 2019, with Immaculate Kassait as its first commissioner from 2020](<https://techtrendske.co.ke/2026/09/30/kenya-data-protection-commissioner-shortlist/>). By March 2025 it had [received 7,128 complaints, issued 215 determinations and penalised 10 entities](<https://www.odpc.go.ke/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/ODPC-Data-Bulletin-12th-Edition.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the outgoing commissioner [counted 459 determinations in six years, with enforcement action against the Ministry of Agriculture and Migori County Assembly](<https://techtrendske.co.ke/2026/11/13/kenya-data-protection-law-ai-regulation/>). She [leaves on 16 November 2026 after six years](<https://www.kbc.co.ke/kassait-calls-for-reforms-central-data-pool-as-she-exits-data-protection-office/>). A [successor was nominated on 10 November](<https://techtrendske.co.ke/2026/11/13/kenya-data-protection-law-ai-regulation/>). On 8 September 2026 [Citizen Digital reported that Kenya had not yet formally joined the Malabo Convention](<https://citizen.digital/article/stakeholders-urge-ratification-of-malabo-convention-for-effective-digital-governance-in-kenya-n389789>).

Liberia's printed [Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act](<https://mopt.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/An_Act_For_The_Collection_Processing_-Transmission_-Storage_-Protection_-And_Use_Of_Personal-_Information_In_Liberia_Printed_Version_20260323_063904.pdf>) was approved on 9 March 2026 and printed on 23 March 2026. It takes effect on publication into handbills. In the last twelve months, on 13 September 2026 the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection [said](<https://smartnewsliberia.com/mgcsp-admits-authentic-beneficiary-data-leaked-launches-internal-investigation/>) that it is aware of its responsibilities under the Act. The Act gives data protection functions to the Independent Information Commissioner, created by the Freedom of Information Act of 2010. It does not state that the Commissioner has begun acting under it. No ratification of the Malabo Convention has been found, and no appointed authority. Establishing would need ratification of the Malabo Convention or an appointed authority.

[Libya's National AI Strategy, adopted on 1 June 2026, says that the Data Protection and Privacy Law is still in draft](<https://smex.org/libyas-new-ai-strategy-celebrates-participation-yet-was-built-without-it/>). It sets the law's adoption as a 2026 target. [SMEX reported in July 2026 that Libya has no functioning data protection authority](<https://smex.org/libyas-new-ai-strategy-celebrates-participation-yet-was-built-without-it/>). The [African Union status list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records no signature and no ratification by Libya. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No data protection law in force has been found, and no authority. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

Lesotho [enacted its Data Protection Act in 2011](<https://digitalrightsalliance.africa/exploring-the-data-protection-and-data-governance-challenges-and-opportunities-in-lesotho/>). The Act provides for a Data Protection Commission. No change has been found in the last twelve months. [Cenfri says](<https://cenfri.org/articles/african-data-governance-reform-in-an-era-of-reform/>) the Commission had not been appointed by 23 March 2026, and an [article of 27 March 2026](<https://digitalrightsalliance.africa/exploring-the-data-protection-and-data-governance-challenges-and-opportunities-in-lesotho/>) says no independent body exists to enforce the law. The [African Union status list](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) of 2 February 2026 records that Lesotho ratified or acceded to the Malabo Convention on 5 February 2025. Operating would need an appointed authority that has registered organisations, taken breach reports, issued guidance or inspected in the past three years.

The president of the CNDP, interviewed on 4 August 2026, [speaks of Law 09-08](<https://fnh.ma/article/actualite-economique/protection-donnes-confiance-moteur-economique-numerique>) as in force for more than fifteen years. The CNDP, Morocco's national commission for the control of personal data protection, [validated five new deliberations](<https://www.cndp.ma/la-cndp-publie-de-nouvelles-deliberations/>) on 28 November 2025. In the last twelve months, in a communiqué dated 28 August 2026 it [gave guidance](<https://fr.walaw.press/country/cirdi/QWSP/articles/legislatives_2026_la_cndp_encadre_l_usage_des_donnees_personnelles_et_de_l_ia_pendant_la_campagne/GPFLSXGWQQFM>) on Law 09-08 to political parties and voters for the 23 September 2026 elections. It also opened a 3020 information line. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

Loi n° 2014-038 on the protection of personal data was [promulgated on 9 January 2015](<https://digital.gov.mg/en/2022/07/05/loi-n-2014-038-sur-la-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel/>). Seven members of the Commission Malagasy de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CMIL) were [sworn in at the Cour suprême on 4 August 2025](<https://assemblee-nationale.mg/article/prestation-de-serment-des-membres-de-la-commission-malagasy-de-linformatique-et-des-libertes-cmil/>). In the last twelve months, in March 2026 the Unité de Gouvernance Digitale [announced the CMIL is now effectively in place](<https://digital.gov.mg/en/2026/03/27/rapport-annuel-sur-la-confidentialiteet-la-protection-des-donnees-a-madagascar/>). The CMIL's [annual report of January 2026](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/11XR_I-6z6Y28qnrEjHABu3SOIbjWy6yW/view>) says no processing declaration has been registered yet, and that the commission has no premises or staff. No source dated in the last three years shows it issuing guidance or inspecting. Operating would need an appointed authority that has registered organisations, taken breach reports, issued guidance or inspected in the past three years.

Law no. 2013-015 of 21 May 2013, as amended, is the basis the authority's president [cited for its sanctions when opening its session on 3 August 2026](<https://orbiteinfo.com/mali-lapdp-ouvre-sa-2e-session-2026-avec-1-000-dossiers-au-programme/>). In 2025 the Autorité de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (APDP) [fined a Bamako clinic 5 million FCFA](<https://fr.apanews.net/community/mali-lapdp-examine-2-000-dossiers-et-un-projet-darrete/>) for obstructing a verification mission. It also [fined Société Aminata Konaté SARL 5 million F CFA](<https://malijet.com/les_faits_divers_au_mali/303061-sanction-pour-non-respect-des-donnees-personnelles--penalite-de-.html>) for refusing one. In the last twelve months, it opened a [Ségou antenna on 4 December 2025](<https://lessor.ml/posts/autorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-la-region-de-segou-a-son-antenne-6932a107b56bd>). It held its [second ordinary session on 3 August 2026](<https://orbiteinfo.com/mali-lapdp-ouvre-sa-2e-session-2026-avec-1-000-dossiers-au-programme/>) under president Pr Mamoudou Samassekou.

[DLA Piper states](<https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/guide.pdf?c=MZ>) that Mozambique has no specific data protection legislation, in a guide last modified on 17 February 2026. The World Bank says the Data Protection Act had [not been approved by Cabinet or submitted to Parliament as of October 2025](<https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099012626175535228>). In the last twelve months, on 1 October 2026 the Assembly's Standing Commission [placed a draft law on the agenda of the session opening 28 October](<https://clubofmozambique.com/news/mozambique-parliament-convenes-extraordinary-and-ordinary-sessions-for-october/>). A [review of the draft law](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-mozambiques-proposed-personal-data-protection-law>) says it designates the existing Regulatory Authority for ICT as the National Authority. [Mozambique ratified the Malabo Convention on 2 December 2019](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>). No law in force and no appointed authority has been found. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

Mauritania's Law 2017-020 of 22 July 2017 on personal data protection is applied in the authority's [deliberation 002/2026 of 24 March 2026](<https://www.apd.mr/%d8%a7%d9%84%d9%85%d8%af%d8%a7%d9%88%d9%84%d8%a9-%d8%b1%d9%82%d9%85002-2026-%d8%aa%d8%aa%d8%b6%d9%85%d9%86-%d8%b1%d8%a3%d9%8a%d8%a7-%d8%a8%d8%ae%d8%b5%d9%88%d8%b5-%d9%85%d9%82%d8%b1%d8%b1-%d9%85/>). In the last twelve months, the Autorité de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (APD) approved amendments to its transfer and cloud deliberations at its [29 April 2026 meeting](<https://www.apd.mr/fr/reunion-mensuelle-ordinaire-de-lautorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-16/>). It held its [ordinary monthly session on 30 June 2026](<https://www.apd.mr/fr/reunion-mensuelle-ordinaire-de-lautorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-18/>). Its [president was sworn in for a second term on 7 October 2026](<https://rimweb.net/2026/10/08/le-president-de-lautorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-prete-serment-pour-un-second-mandat/>). No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

The Data Protection Office [reports on its 2024 enforcement](<https://dataprotection.govmu.org/AnnualReports/265-26-DPO%20AR%202024-SOFT%20COPY.pdf>) of the Data Protection Act 2017, and has been [operational since 16 February 2009](<https://dataprotection.govmu.org/AnnualReports/265-26-DPO%20AR%202024-SOFT%20COPY.pdf>). For 2024 it [reports](<https://dataprotection.govmu.org/AnnualReports/265-26-DPO%20AR%202024-SOFT%20COPY.pdf>) 179 new complaints and 39 closed. In the last twelve months, in January 2026 it [co-led the launch of the National Data Strategy 2025-2029](<https://lexpress.mu/node/553938>) with the ministry. In September 2026 it [told management companies to register as controllers and name their own officers](<https://dataprotection.govmu.org/Documents/Advice%20to%20%20MCs%20on%20Registration.pdf>). On 29 October 2026 the Minister [said 23,000 of some 60,000 entities required to register had done so](<https://lexpress.mu/node/564216>). No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

Malawi's Data Protection Act, 2024 [was assented to on 31 January 2024 and published on 2 February 2024](<https://www.mca.ac.mw/mca-siteup/uploads/Data%20Protection%20Act%202024.pdf>). [The Authority's compliance guideline](<https://www.dpa.mw/download/guideline-and-checklist-on-compliance/?wpdmdl=8808>) says other Malawi controllers and processors had to comply from 3 June 2026. The [guidelines state](<https://www.dpa.mw/download/guidelines-on-personal-data-breach-notifications-and-communications/?wpdmdl=8818>) that MACRA is the designated Data Protection Authority under the Act. In the last twelve months, [Nyasa Times](<https://www.nyasatimes.com/macra-consults-stakeholders-on-proposed-data-protection-registration-fees/>) reports it convened a stakeholder consultation on draft regulations in Lilongwe in July 2026. [In November 2026 MACRA, as the Authority, held a workshop in Blantyre on proposed registration fees](<https://www.dpa.mw/dpa-reviews-proposed-data-protection-registration-fees/>). No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

[Minister Theofelus said on 14 August 2025](<https://thebrief.com.na/2025/08/namibias-data-protection-bill-to-be-tabled-in-september/>) that the ministry would table a Data Protection Bill in September 2025. In the last twelve months the position changed: [Minister Theofelus said in July 2026](<https://itweb.africa/article/namibia-pushes-cyber-security-reforms/mQwkoq6YJWlM3r9A>) that Namibia is finalising the bill. An opposition MP told the Windhoek Observer in August 2026 that [Namibia has no data protection statute](<https://observer24.com.na/mp-raises-concerns-about-data-control-of-smart-city-grant-from-china/>). Namibia [ratified the Malabo Convention on 25 January 2019](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>). No law in force, no appointed authority and no activity by one has been found. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

The president of the HAPDP said in an interview published on 28 July 2025 that [law no. 2022-59 of 16 December 2022](<https://www.lesahel.org/entretien-avec-le-president-de-la-haute-autorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-hapdp/>) repealed and replaced the 2017 law. The authority's [consolidated text of April 2026](<https://www.hapdp.ne/uploads/files/Loi-2022-59-consolidee.pdf>) presents it as the operative general law. In the last twelve months, [Africa Data Protection reports](<https://www.africadataprotection.org/actualites/Niger-Suppression-de-la-Haute-Autorite-de-Protection-des-Donnees-a-caractere-Personnel-et-transfert-de-ses-competences.html>), in a report published on 13 June 2026, that the government has abolished the HAPDP by decree. It split the HAPDP's powers between the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of the Interior. No authority appointed after the decree has been found. Operating would need an appointed authority that has registered organisations, taken breach reports, issued guidance or inspected in the past three years.

The [Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023](<https://www.digitalbusiness.africa/donnees-nigeria-letat-reprend-la-ndpc-apres-plus-de-9-millions-de-recettes-generees-en-3-ans/>) was signed by President Tinubu on 12 June 2023. The Commission [fined Multichoice Nigeria N766,242,500](<https://www.rapdp.org/index.php/en/node/222>) in 2025 for violating the Act. In the last twelve months, in February 2026 it [served a compliance notice on 649 higher-education institutions](<https://businessday.ng/bd-weekender/article/nigerias-data-protection-audit-return-blessing-udo-advocates-emulation/>). A [federal circular dated 27 July 2026](<https://www.thecable.ng/fg-directs-mdas-to-appoint-data-protection-officers-comply-with-ndp-act/>) directed all federal ministries, departments and agencies to comply with it. In August 2026 the Commission [opened an investigation](<https://dailytrust.com/ndpc-investigates-varsity-bank-over-data-violations/>) into Hackerbella Ltd, the University of Lagos and Lotus Bank. In October 2026 its National Commissioner said [41,000 organisations had registered with the Commission in 2026](<https://businessday.ng/interview/article/protection-of-personal-privacy-and-rights-is-central-to-ndpcs-mandate-olatunji/>).

Rwanda's [Data Protection Act was introduced on 15 October 2021](<https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/32861/opinions/why-2026-is-the-year-of-accountability-for-data-controllers-and-processors>), and its two-year grace period ended on 15 October 2023. The National Cyber Security Authority [acts as the supervisory authority](<https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/32861/opinions/why-2026-is-the-year-of-accountability-for-data-controllers-and-processors>) for data protection under the Act. In the last twelve months, [The New Times](<https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/32861/opinions/why-2026-is-the-year-of-accountability-for-data-controllers-and-processors>) reported in January 2026 that the Authority has registered data controllers and processors over four years. It has trained over 100 public sector data protection officers. In July 2026 [CIPESA](<https://cipesa.org/2026/07/rethinking-africas-approach-to-the-politics-of-ai-governance-and-regulation/>) said Rwanda's AI policy gives it oversight of data protection in AI systems. No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

The [Sudanese Center for Policy Studies](<https://sudancps.com/en/2026/07/19/sudans-privacy-gap-balancing-digital-transformation-and-data-laws-intro/>) says Sudan has no privacy law governing personal data, and that a 2018 draft bill was never enacted. In the last twelve months, on 6 August 2026 the Council of Ministers [discussed a draft data and artificial intelligence bill](<https://sudantribune.net/article/317108>) and directed further study before approval by the interim parliament. The Center says a November 2025 decree established the Sudanese Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority and the Sudanese Cybersecurity Authority. The [same Center](<https://sudancps.com/en/2026/07/19/sudans-privacy-gap-balancing-digital-transformation-and-data-laws-intro/>) says neither had issued binding rules as of mid-2026. Sudan [signed the Malabo Convention on 15 March 2023](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>). Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

A [reference summary](<https://dataprotection.africa/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Senegal-Factsheet.pdf>) states that Senegal's Law No. 2008-12 on the protection of personal data was enacted on 25 January 2008. The Commission de protection des données personnelles (CDP) is an [independent administrative authority](<https://aps.sn/plus-de-300-dossiers-traites-par-la-commission-de-protection-des-donnees-personnelles-au-premier-trimestre-2026-officiel/>) set up by that law. In the last twelve months, on 12 March 2026 the CDP, after a complaint, [inspected Digicommunication International unannounced and ordered the meeting-room camera uninstalled](<https://aps.sn/plus-de-300-dossiers-traites-par-la-commission-de-protection-des-donnees-personnelles-au-premier-trimestre-2026-officiel/>). For April to June 2026 it [reported 195 files handled](<https://www.seneweb.com/fr/news/Societe/donnees-personnelles-plus-de-190-dossiers-traites-par-la-cdp-entre-avril-et-juin_n_503047.html>), 39 authorisations issued and one processing rejected. An expert told [APS](<https://aps.sn/donnees-personnelles-la-legislation-senegalaise-doit-etre-modernisee-et-adaptee-aux-enjeux-de-lia-expert/>) in March 2026 that a bill to replace the law is reportedly in the circuit.

Sierra Leone has a Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill. In [November 2025](<https://sierraloaded.sl/news/government-data-protection-information-bill>) the Information Minister said it had finished its final national validation, with Cabinet and Parliament still to come. In the last twelve months, in [April 2026](<https://moice.gov.sl/cabinet-approves-first-ever-data-protection-policy-paving-way-for-new-data-law/>) Cabinet approved a National Data Protection Policy and authorised a new Data Protection and Right to Access Information Act. The [2025 Bill](<https://sierraloaded.sl/news/government-data-protection-information-bill>) would establish a single independent authority, which is not yet constituted. The [African Union status list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records that Sierra Leone had not ratified the Malabo Convention. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

Somalia's Data Protection Act, Law No. 005 of 2023, was [enacted on 23 March 2023](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-somalias-data-protection-act-and-implementing-regulations>). Somalia [inaugurated its Data Protection Authority on 24 February 2024](<https://blog.africadataprotection.org/en/2024/02/26/somalia-inauguration-of-the-data-protection-authority>). In the last twelve months, its January 2026 [Registration Guidelines](<https://dpa.gov.so/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Registration-Guidelines.pdf>) set fees and a 30-day approval timeline. On 2 June 2026 the Authority [began accepting registration applications](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/06/02/somalia-data-protection-authority-enforces-nationwide-data-compliance-rules/>) from controllers and processors. Its [own service page](<https://dpa.gov.so/services/registration-licensing/>) of the same date lists the registration forms it issues. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

The [World Bank's 2026 diagnostic](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099053126171570627/pdf/P502463-0c06abde-be3d-4f83-b9e1-eca068e7bc1e.pdf>) states there is no national data protection or privacy law in South Sudan. The [ICT Minister said in December 2025](<https://www.radiotamazuj.org/en/news/article/south-sudan-to-get-data-protection-bill-in-2026-says-minister>) the government will introduce its first Data Protection Bill in 2026. In the last twelve months, a workshop of over 30 stakeholders reviewed the [Data Protection Bill, 2025](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/digital-rights-frontlines_dataprotection-digitalrights-cybersecurity-activity-7457423027161620480-l2o_>), according to a post dated 5 May 2026. The [African Union status list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records no signature of the Malabo Convention. No enacted data protection law and no operating authority has been found. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

São Tomé and Príncipe's [Lei n.º 03/2016](<https://www.dataguidance.com/sites/default/files/STP%20-%20Lei%20n.%C2%BA%2003_2016%20-%20Lei%20de%20Garantia%20e%20Protec%C3%A7%C3%A3o%20dos%20Dados%20Pessoais%20d....pdf>) was published in the Diário da República of 10 May 2016. The Agência Nacional de Protecção de Dados Pessoais has a president, José Manuel Costa Alegre. In the last twelve months, in April 2026 he [met the National Assembly president](<https://www.telanon.info/politica/2026/04/15/52530/recenseamento-eleitoral-automatico-vai-ser-fiscalizado-pela-agencia-nacional-de-proteccao-de-dados-pessoais/>) to plan oversight of personal data in the electoral roll. On 1 June 2026 the agency [signed a cooperation memorandum with Macau](<https://www.gov.mo/pt/noticias/831008/>). No source dated in the last three years has been found showing the authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting. Operating would need an appointed authority that has registered organisations, taken breach reports, issued guidance or inspected in the past three years.

Eswatini's [Data Protection Act, 2022](<https://www.esccom.org.sz/legislation/DATA%20PROTECTION%20ACT.pdf>) was gazetted on 4 March 2022. The [notice of 2024](<https://edpa.org.sz/assets/documents/EDPA%20NOTICE%201%202024%20-%20FINAL%20DECISION%20ON%20THE%20REGISTRATION%20OF%20DATA%20CONTROLLERS%20AND%20DATA%20PROCESSORS.pdf>) states the Act designates the Eswatini Communications Commission as the Eswatini Data Protection Authority. The Authority issued [enforcement notices under section 41 in June 2024 to MTN Eswatini and Liberty Life Swaziland Limited](<https://www.edpa.org.sz/enforcement.html>). It issued another [in March 2025 to the Royal Science Technology Park](<https://www.edpa.org.sz/enforcement.html>). In the last twelve months, in June 2026 it [opened a formal investigation into the Ministry of Home Affairs](<https://independentnews.co.sz/45057/news/home-affairs-investigated-for-for-sensitive-data-breach/>). In September 2026 it was [led by an acting chief executive](<https://eswatinipositivenews.online/edpa-takes-data-protection-services-closer-to-emaswati/>).

Seychelles' [Data Protection Act, 2023](<https://www.gazette.sc/sites/default/files/2023-12/Act%2024%20-%202023%20-%20Data%20Protection%20Act%202023.pdf>) was assented to on 19 December 2023 and bears the operative date 22 December 2023. The [Information Commission](<https://www.gazette.sc/sites/default/files/2023-12/Act%2024%20-%202023%20-%20Data%20Protection%20Act%202023.pdf>) is named in section 5 as the competent authority. In the last twelve months, in 2026 it [marked Data Protection Day with guidance to organisations and the public](<https://www.infocom.sc/data-protection-day-2026-building-trust-in-a-digital-seychelles/>). In 2025 it [handled 14 cases under the Act](<https://www.infocom.sc/wp-content/uploads/Annual-Report-2025.pdf>): 6 on data transfers, 5 breaches, 2 refused deletion requests and 1 consultation. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

Chad's personal data law of 2015 is treated as in force. [A Chadian law firm's analysis published on 6 July 2026 applies Loi n°007/PR/2015 to personal data](<https://thomasd-avocats.com/transfert-international-rapport-enquete-tchad-rgpd/>). [The minister announced on 9 December 2025](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/1012-51293-chad-finalizes-digital-law-to-align-national-framework-with-global-standards>) that authorities were finalising a digital law. In the last twelve months, [Ecofin reported on 16 March 2026](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/1603-53795-chad-approves-reform-strengthening-national-cybersecurity-agency>) that the Senate ratified a reform law on 13 March 2026. It broadens the mandate of ANSICE, the National Agency for Information Security and Electronic Certification, to cover personal data protection. No source has been found showing ANSICE registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting. Operating would need an appointed authority that has registered organisations, taken breach reports, issued guidance or inspected in the past three years.

[Loi n° 2019-014 of 29 October 2019](<https://jo.gouv.tg/sites/default/files/JO/JOS_29_10_2019-64E%20ANNEE-N%C2%B026%20TER.pdf>) on personal data protection was adopted by the National Assembly and promulgated. The IPDCP [officially launched its activities in Lomé on 28 March 2025](<https://www.togofirst.com/fr/tic/2903-16040-numerique-l-instance-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-demarre-ses-activites>). In the last twelve months, it [ran a three-day training for 35 data protection correspondents from 22 to 24 June 2026](<https://ipdcp.tg/lipdcp-lance-la-premiere-session-de-formation-des-correspondants-a-la-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel/>). On 15 September 2026 it [convened a compliance meeting for public administrations](<https://levisionnaire.tg/protection-des-donnees-lipdcp-appelle-les-administrations-togolaises-a-accelerer-leur-mise-en-conformite/>). [On 18 November 2026 it certified the first 28, from banks, insurers, telecom operators and local authorities among others](<https://ipdcp.tg/protection-des-donnees-personnelles-28-correspondants-certifies-par-lipdcp/>). No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

Organic law no. 2004-63 of 27 July 2004 sets the [general processing, consent and rights regime](<https://legislation-securite.tn/latest-laws/loi-organique-n-2004-63-du-27-juillet-2004-portant-sur-la-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel/>). A replacement bill, no. 095/2025, was [deposited before the Assembly on 14 July 2025](<https://www.arp.tn/loi/project/4237>). The [Government decree no. 2021-230 of 16 April 2021](<https://legislation-securite.tn/ar/latest-laws/%D8%A3%D9%85%D8%B1-%D8%AD%D9%83%D9%88%D9%85%D9%8A-%D8%B9%D8%AF%D8%AF-230-%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%86%D8%A9-2021-%D9%85%D8%A4%D8%B1%D8%AE-%D9%81%D9%8A-16-%D8%A3%D9%81%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%84-2021-%D9%8A%D8%AA%D8%B9/>) appointed twelve named members to the national personal data protection authority. In the last twelve months, the Forum Chawki Gaddes issued a [statement on 3 October 2026](<https://businessnews.com.tn/2026/10/04/le-forum-chawki-gaddes-denonce-la-divulgation-de-donnees-personnelles-et-appelle-a-proteger-les-mineurs/1421336/>) saying the activities of the authority, INPDP, are at a standstill. No source dated in the last three years has been found showing the authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting. Operating would need an appointed authority that has done one of those things in the past three years.

The [Personal Data Protection Act, Chapter 44, commenced on 1 May 2023](<https://www.pdpc.go.tz/media/media/THE_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_ACT.pdf>). [Section 6 of the Act](<https://www.pdpc.go.tz/media/media/THE_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_ACT.pdf>) establishes the Personal Data Protection Commission as a body corporate. A [ruling reported in August 2025](<https://www.rive.co.tz/landmark-ruling-first-pdpc-monetary-award-signals-new-era-for-personal-data-in-tanzania/>) awarded TZS 20,000,000 against Mi Casa Company Limited. In the last twelve months, The Citizen [reported on 28 August 2026](<https://www.thecitizen.co.tz/tanzania/news/national/data-protection-regulator-begins-compliance-crackdown-5574710>) that the Commission will inspect compliance with the Act from 31 August 2026. [PDPC figures cited in October 2026](<https://www.therespondents.co.tz/2026/10/pdpc-bolsters-safeguards-as-personal.html>) show 15,146 institutions registered and 445 complaints received by August 2026.

Uganda's Personal Data Protection Office [applied the Data Protection and Privacy Act, Cap 97, in its decision of 18 July 2025](<https://pdpo.go.ug/media/2025/07/Ssekamwa-Frank-3-Ors-vs-Google-LLC-PDPO-Decision-18th-July-2024.pdf>). On [18 July 2025 it found Google in breach](<https://pdpo.go.ug/media/2025/07/Ssekamwa-Frank-3-Ors-vs-Google-LLC-PDPO-Decision-18th-July-2024.pdf>) and ordered it to register within 30 days. In the last twelve months, the [PDPO's decision of 20 February 2026](<https://businesstimesug.com/whatsapp-updates-privacy-policies-after-uganda-data-protection-enforcement/>) partly upheld a complaint against WhatsApp LLC and Meta Platforms and issued corrective orders. On 17 July 2026 it confirmed WhatsApp had implemented them. In July 2026 the Office [supervised more than 13,400 registered data controllers and processors](<https://ict.go.ug/media/news/familiarisation-visit-highlights-nita-us-digital-progress>). It [briefed government IT officers](<https://techreviewafrica.purplealmondconsulting.com/public/news/6726/uganda-personal-data-protection-office-engages-information-technology-officers-from-government-ministries>) on data protection on 13 August 2026.

[South Africa's data protection law came into force on 1 July 2021](<https://www.itweb.co.za/article/inforeg-unpacks-regulatory-complexities-posed-by-ai/KA3WwMdzPryvrydZ>). [The African Union's list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records that South Africa signed the Malabo Convention on 16 February 2023, with no ratification. The Information Regulator [has received over 8,000 reports of security compromises](<https://www.itweb.co.za/article/inforeg-concerned-by-alarming-rate-of-data-breaches/rxP3jqBE2ZLMA2ye>), 1,220 of them since April 2026. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, it [gave the South African Bureau of Standards 90 days](<https://www.itweb.co.za/article/inforeg-concerned-by-alarming-rate-of-data-breaches/rxP3jqBE2ZLMA2ye>) to revise its policies and put security measures in place. No bill or draft has been found for the planned amendment of the law on artificial intelligence.

A [World Bank tender notice of 10 August 2026](<https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/procurement-detail/OP00461500>) treats Zambia's Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 as the law being implemented. The first Data Protection Commissioner was [appointed in June 2023](<https://www.itnewsafrica.com/2025/04/zambias-data-protection-commissioner-fully-operational-enforcing-privacy-compliance/>). The Commissioner's office [opened online registration](<https://www.itnewsafrica.com/2025/04/zambias-data-protection-commissioner-fully-operational-enforcing-privacy-compliance/>) for controllers and processors, with a 30 April 2025 deadline. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

Zimbabwe's Cyber and Data Protection Act [Chapter 12:07] is applied through SI 155 of 2024, which [took effect in September 2024](<https://techunzipped.co.zw/2026/08/potraz-to-begin-mandatory-data-protection-compliance-inspections-from-1-september-2026/>) and made a Data Controller Licence mandatory. [POTRAZ states](<https://postonsunday.co.zw/2026/08/17/potraz-sets-september-deadline-for-data-protection-compliance>) it is the designated Data Protection Authority under section 5 of the Act. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 it [reported 1,123 licence applications so far that year and 1,218 data protection officers trained](<https://www.heraldonline.co.zw/financial-sector-bears-brunt-of-data-breaches-potraz-calls-for-stronger-data-management/>). Its [Regulatory Notice 2 of 2026](<https://postonsunday.co.zw/2026/08/17/potraz-sets-september-deadline-for-data-protection-compliance>) announces mandatory compliance inspections from 1 September 2026. No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.
